projects.title: Milk Run Planner
projects.summary: Packaging data checks → trailer fit → trucks per week per supplier → milk-run routes that consolidate direct FTL lanes. Scenario controls re-optimize the routes live.
projects.result: Real project: 8 FTL lanes from Mexico to Illinois consolidated into a milk run, ~$1M/yr savings. My role: simulation and validation.
projects.readme: Packaging data checks → trailer fit → trucks per week → milk-run routes that consolidate direct FTL lanes (real project: 8 lanes, ~$1M/yr)

projects.title: Shortage Risk
projects.summary: Red-parts early warning: planning days-on-hand cross-checked with actual goods issues, so forecast-zeroed or "obsolete" parts that are still being consumed can't hide. One ranked list, linked to bin locations.
projects.result: Built after an end-of-production shortage and customer escalation. Local prototype demonstrated, next step is an SAP-integrated build.
projects.readme: Red-parts early warning: planning DOH cross-checked with actual issues, one ranked risk list linked to bin locations

projects.title: RackScan
projects.summary: Rack damage on a 3D warehouse layout: tap the damaged upright or beam, log it with a photo and a priority, and track it until it is repaired.
projects.result: An in-house alternative to a ~$15K/yr inspection subscription. Demonstrated to the site director, replacement planned at contract end.
projects.readme: Rack damage on a 3D warehouse layout: point to the damaged upright or beam, log it with a photo, track the repair

projects.title: WMS LX03 Viewer
projects.summary: Turns the flat SAP LX03 bin-stock report into a warehouse map: where every part is, how many HUs it has, how old it is, and which stock is blocked.
projects.result: For a 2,000+ SKU warehouse, finding parts and problem stock felt about 10× faster in daily use.
projects.readme: SAP WM bin stock as a warehouse map: where every part is, how many HUs, how old

projects.title: Engine Line Andon
projects.summary: 4 assembly lines × 6 stations. Operator badge + base-engine QR scan opens a work instruction with a timer; wrong-line engines or parts lock the station until the supervisor fixes them; Quality / Maintenance / Material calls hit the office board instantly and hide Finish until the right responder scans in.
projects.result: Real system I built and maintained (engine assembly, 2015–2020): about 20% less downtime once calls reached managers and engineers the moment they were pressed. Serial-level traceability and an improvement checklist built from the call log.
projects.readme: 4 lines × 6 stations: scan-gated work instructions, wrong-engine/part lockout, andon calls on the office board, engine traceability (real system: ~20% less downtime)

projects.title: Pull Pack-out Planner
projects.tag: Pull Scheduling · Cycle Counting · Curing Room
projects.summary: EPP parts cure 12–24 h, then are packed and shuttled to a warehouse in another building. Parts below 2 days on hand with an urgent OEM sequence go on a targeted cycle count; racks are then packed in the order warehouse stock runs out, back-scheduled from customer lead time and the shuttle schedule. Overstocked parts stay in the curing room.
projects.result: Real change (EPP plant, 2010–2015), planned with the team and implemented by me: the warehouse held at about 90% instead of overflowing, and the curing room ran the second shift from the printed plan without adding indirect labor.
projects.readme: Targeted cycle count + pull pack-out order for an EPP curing room (real change: warehouse held ~90%, no added indirect labor)
